1. Overview of Acts
 1) What Acts is about
 - 'Praxeis Apostolon' - the footsteps of the apostles.
사도들의 발자취라 하지만 12 사도의 이야기가 다 나와 있지는 않고 앞부: It's called the footsteps of the apostles, but it doesn't tell the story of all twelve apostles. The first part shows what Peter did, centered on Jerusalem, then Philip's work in Samaria, and then the ministry of Paul and Barnabas in Antioch.
그 뒤에는 사도 바울과 바나바의 첫 번째 선교여행, 그리고 바울의 두 번:
After that it covers the first missionary journey of the apostle Paul and Barnabas, then Paul's second and third missionary journeys, and all the way to his road to Rome.
 - Acts is a book of transition. It shows the shift from the age of God the Father in the Old Testament and the age of God the Son, Jesus, in the Gospels, to the age of God the Holy Spirit.
 - When Jesus ascended, He told His disciples, "But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judaea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth." Acts shows how that word comes true.
 - It's really spectacular. So much so that you could call it the Acts of the Holy Spirit. It's the story of the gospel spreading, with the Holy Spirit in charge, taking hold of people like Peter and Paul. Don't look at Peter or Paul. Look at what the Holy Spirit is doing.
 2) Author: Luke
 - He writes it like a sequel to the Gospel of Luke.
<행1:1~2> 데오빌로여 내가 먼저 쓴 글에는 무릇 예수의 행하시며 가:
<Acts 1:1~2> The former treatise have I made, O Theophilus, of all that Jesus began both to do and teach, until the day in which he was taken up, after that he through the Holy Ghost had given commandments unto the apostles whom he had chosen:
 - Same recipient, and he says he's picking up where his earlier writing left off, recording the footsteps of the apostles after Jesus' ascension.
 3) How it relates to Paul's letters
 - It's connected to ten letters: 1 & 2 Thessalonians, Galatians, 1 & 2 Corinthians, Romans, and the Prison Epistles.
 - As you read Acts, you need to look at things like this: Paul stayed somewhere and worked for a few years; during that time, what letter did he write, whose hands did he put it in, and where did he send it? After the letter was read aloud, how did the people who heard it react? And what follow-up steps were taken because of that?
 - If you read them separately, they're hard to understand. They're letters, after all... The more you know about what went on between the sender and the recipients, the better off you are.
 4) Why we study Acts
 - Studying the early history of Christianity and the early church gives us models and cases to learn from.
 - It's the textbook for every missionary.
 - We are all missionaries. So we need to study our textbook, Acts, well.
오순절 성령 강림: The Holy Spirit comes at Pentecost
<행1:5> 요한은 물로 세례를 베풀었으나 너희는 몇 날이 못되어 성령으:
<Acts 1:5> For John truly baptized with water; but ye shall be baptized with the Holy Ghost not many days hence.
 - The word baptism is baptizo, which means to be immersed in water. It's closer to the meaning of immersion.
 - Three meanings of baptism, or immersion
 ① Washing away sin: the point isn't being dunked in water, it's washing away sin.
 ②  Dying: the old self is buried with Jesus.
 ③ Being united: being united with Jesus.

It means leaving room for God to make the decision.
3. 오순절 성령 강림: 3. The Holy Spirit Comes at Pentecost
<행2:1~4> 오순절 날이 이미 이르매 저희가 다 같이 한 곳에 모였더:
<Acts 2:1~4> And when the day of Pentecost was fully come, they were all with one accord in one place. And there appeared unto them cloven tongues like as of fire, and it sat upon each of them. And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance.
 - This is a special case that happened just once. It's not a general, everyday event.
 - The word for "tongues" in the Bible is, in most places, more correctly translated "foreign languages."
<행2:5~11> 그 때에 경건한 유대인이 천하 각국으로부터 와서 예루살:

 - The people who gathered then had come from all over the world to keep the feast, before Passover, before Jesus was nailed to the cross. 그러니까 이 부분을 읽을 때 주인공은 방언이 아니고 각 사람들이 말씀을: So when you read this part, the main thing isn't the tongues. It's that each person heard the word and was cut to the heart.
<행2:37~39> 형제들아 우리가 어찌할꼬 하거늘 (자기가 죄인임을 깨: <Acts 2:37~39> Men and brethren, what shall we do? <행2:43~47> 사람마다 두려워하는데 사도들로 인하여 기사와 표적이:
<Acts 2:43~47> And fear came upon every soul: and many wonders and signs were done by the apostles. And they, continuing daily with one accord in the temple, and breaking bread from house to house, did eat their meat with gladness and singleness of heart, Praising God, and having favour with all the people. And the Lord added to the church daily such as should be saved.
 - You could misunderstand this as a picture of the ideal church, but it's not a model. It's a special case. The Jerusalem church back then was in a situation where it had no other choice.
 1) Jerusalem wasn't an industrial city; it was a political and religious city.
 -  If you believed in Jesus, you were thrown out of Judaism, had to leave every public office, and business deals were cut off. So to make a living, you had no choice but to sell your property and use the money to buy food.
나중에 바울이 어딜가나 교회를 개척하면 예루살렘의 성도를 위해서 연보 하:
Later, wherever Paul goes and plants a church, you see him saying, "Let's take up an offering for the saints in Jerusalem. We heard the spiritual gospel from Jerusalem, so it's right to serve them with material things," and he's always carrying it back there.
 - But the Jerusalem church did well to do it that way. Because they had no property, they scattered in every direction, and that's why they didn't die when Jerusalem was destroyed in A.D 70.
 - Even so, in the end the number of people gradually dropped, and some went back to Judaism, and the letter written to people like that is Hebrews.

33절 내가 곧 당신에게 사람을 보내었는데 오셨으니 잘하였나이다. 이제: Verse 33. Immediately therefore I sent to thee; and thou hast well done that thou art come. Now therefore are we all here present before God, to hear all things that are commanded thee of God.
자세가 딱 되어 있죠? 주께서 당신에게 명하신 모든 것을 듣고자 하여 누: That's exactly the right attitude, isn't it? To hear all things commanded thee of God, they are present before whom? Before God... Is it true that you, too, are present before God to hear all things commanded to Evangelist Seong-jong Baek?
그래서 베드로가 예수님에 대해서 쭉 설명을 합니다. 그 때 성령께서 갑자: So Peter explains all about Jesus. Then the Holy Spirit suddenly comes down.
<행10:44~48> 베드로가 이 말 할 때에 성령이 말씀 듣는 모든 사:
<Acts 10:44~48> While Peter yet spake these words, the Holy Ghost fell on all them which heard the word. And they of the circumcision which believed were astonished, as many as came with Peter, because that on the Gentiles also was poured out the gift of the Holy Ghost. For they heard them speak with tongues, and magnify God. Then answered Peter, Can any man forbid water, that these should not be baptized, which have received the Holy Ghost as well as we? And he commanded them to be baptized in the name of the Lord. Then prayed they him to tarry certain days.
 4) Unusually, the Holy Spirit comes down in the middle of the sermon. So Peter says, why hesitate to baptize with water people who have received the baptism of the Holy Spirit? and baptizes them.
그래서 이방인 들에게도 성령이 임하시는 이 특이한 경험을 베드로가 예루살: So Peter reports this unusual experience - the Holy Spirit coming on Gentiles too - to the Jerusalem church.
<행11:1~3> 유대에 있는 사도들과 형제들이 이방인들도 하나님 말씀을:
<Acts 11:1~3> And the apostles and brethren that were in Judaea heard that the Gentiles had also received the word of God. And when Peter was come up to Jerusalem, they that were of the circumcision contended with him, Saying, Thou wentest in to men uncircumcised, and didst eat with them.
 5) He's talking about the important matter that the Holy Spirit comes on Gentiles too, and ridiculously, it's: "Why did you go into the house of uncircumcised Gentiles?" That's the kind of church the Jerusalem church was.
그 때 베드로가 이방인들에게 성령이 내려왔다는 은혜 받은 이야기를 하니까: Then when Peter tells the grace-filled story of the Holy Spirit coming down on the Gentiles, the question of 'whether we can eat in Gentile homes from now on' quietly disappears, and in verse 18 they say God has granted the Gentiles repentance unto life too, and gloss right over it. We do that sometimes too, don't we?
11. 안디옥 교회의 성장: 11. The Growth of the Antioch Church
<행11:19~24> 때에 스데반의 일로 일어난 환난을 인하여 흩어진 자:
<Acts 11:19~24> Now they which were scattered abroad upon the persecution that arose about Stephen travelled as far as Phenice, and Cyprus, and Antioch, preaching the word to none but unto the Jews only. And some of them were men of Cyprus and Cyrene, which, when they were come to Antioch, spake unto the Grecians, preaching the Lord Jesus. And the hand of the Lord was with them: and a great number believed, and turned unto the Lord. Then tidings of these things came unto the ears of the church which was in Jerusalem: and they sent forth Barnabas, that he should go as far as Antioch. Who, when he came, and had seen the grace of God, was glad, and exhorted them all, that with purpose of heart they would cleave unto the Lord. For he was a good man, and full of the Holy Ghost and of faith: and much people was added unto the Lord.
 1) At this time a few of the scattered people went as far as Antioch and preached the gospel, and a church was born. So the Jerusalem church sent Barnabas to Antioch. They did well. But this Barnabas isn't called a smart man; Barnabas was a good man. A church planter or evangelist has to be good. Someone who isn't good shouldn't rush out claiming to do the Lord's work. Character matters more than anything else.
<행11:25~26> 바나바가 사울을 찾으러 다소에 가서 만나매 안디옥에:
<Acts 11:25~26> Then departed Barnabas to Tarsus, for to seek Saul: And when he had found him, he brought him unto Antioch. And it came to pass, that a whole year they assembled themselves with the church, and taught much people. And the disciples were called Christians first in Antioch.
 2) They didn't do something else; they taught. The Bible at this time was the Old Testament.
 3) They lived just like Christ, so they got the nickname Christians. Actually it was a slightly mocking expression, but today Christians live so differently from the Bible that they've picked up an insulting nickname in Korea, "gaedokgyo" (roughly "dog-Christianity"). That's something to think about.
12. 야고보의 순교와 베드로의 풀려남: 12. The Martyrdom of James and Peter's Release
<행12:1~3> 그 때에 헤롯왕이 손을 들어 교회 중 몇 사람을 해하려:
<Acts 12:1~3> Now about that time Herod the king stretched forth his hands to vex certain of the church. And he killed James the brother of John with the sword. And because he saw it pleased the Jews, he proceeded further to take Peter also. (Then were the days of unleavened bread.)
 1) The Herod here is Herod Agrippa I. James becomes the first to be martyred. Seeing that this pleased the Jews, Herod arrests and imprisons Peter too, but Peter is spared. Why did God let James die and spare Peter? We don't know, but there have to be people who hold on to the truth even at the cost of their lives, and there also have to be people who remain. Martyrdom, evangelism, and witness are the same word. Martyrio.
 2) When proud Herod gave a speech and the people exalted him, he didn't give the glory to God, so God struck him and he died, but the word kept growing and multiplying.
사도행전 곳곳에 결론적으로 나오는 말씀은 '많은 사람들이 주께로 돌아오더: The words that come up again and again across Acts as a conclusion are 'many turned to the Lord' and 'the word of God grew mightily and prevailed.' Healings, receiving gifts like tongues, even miracles like dead people coming back to life - those things aren't important in themselves. We need to pay more attention to what God accomplished through them. The apostles, the earliest missionaries, didn't do anything else; they taught the word (the Old Testament) and helped people realize that Jesus is the Christ. We need to do this kind of ministry too.
